findings.issue: Round 1 (reality-batch1-review.json) found the tech-spec's stale full-suite baseline '1626 passed, 441 subtests' hallucinated into Tasks 1-3, and Tasks 1/2/3 were corrected to the measured '1693 passed, 462 subtests (замерено на 3362f26, 2026-08-05)'. That fix was not propagated to the rest of the decomposition: Task 4's Verification Steps still says 'база 1626 passed / 441 subtests, регрессов нет' (tasks/4.md:152) with no caveat. The same uncorrected '1626 passed' (sometimes with '441 subtests') appears in Task 5 (Acceptance Criteria + Verification Steps, tasks/5.md:213,251), Task 7 (tasks/7.md:185,223), Task 8 (tasks/8.md:316), Task 9 (tasks/9.md:178,220), and in Task 10's prose (tasks/10.md:205). I independently reran the full suite on the current branch point and confirmed the real number is 1693 passed / 462 subtests (matches Task 13's re-measurement claim exactly). Because 1693 > 1626, a per-task self-check literally worded as '>= 1626 passed' or 'база 1626, регрессов нет' will PASS even if that task's own change silently regressed the suite down to anywhere between 1627 and 1692 -- the stale number doesn't just look outdated, it weakens each of these five tasks' own regression gate during execution. (Task 13's independent re-measurement at the end of Phase 1 is unaffected and remains a safe final gate, but mid-pipeline the per-task checks in 4/5/7/8/9/10 are not measuring what they claim to measure.)
findings.fix: Replace the stale '1626 passed / 441 subtests' in tasks/4.md:152, tasks/5.md:213+251, tasks/7.md:185+223, tasks/8.md:316, tasks/9.md:178+220, and tasks/10.md:205 with either the measured '1693 passed / 462 subtests (замерено на 3362f26, 2026-08-05)' (matching how Tasks 1/2/3 were fixed), or with Task 6's safer wording ('сравнивать надо со своим прогоном, а не с числом') that tells the executor to capture a fresh baseline rather than trust a hardcoded figure.

findings.issue: Task 6 and Task 7 are both in Wave 3 (parallel, no depends_on between them) and both plan to touch t_hunted_source.py. Task 7's whole job is to gut and rewrite the paragraph-building, boilerplate-filter, subtitle-lift and image-collection logic of that 257-line file (tasks/7.md Files table: lines 195-199, 201-205, 216-220, 226-250 all rewritten). Task 6's Implementation hints (tasks/6.md ~line 432-436) explicitly offer an optional path where the executor adds a one-line public alias for `_IMAGE_LIMIT` directly in t_hunted_source.py ('если решишь сделать имя публичным — это однострочный алиас в t_hunted_source.py... отметь его в отчёте как расширение объёма') -- i.e. the task text itself proposes editing a file that a parallel same-wave task is simultaneously rewriting wholesale, and neither task's Dependencies/Edge-cases section cross-references the other regarding this file. This is inconsistent with how the rest of this decomposition handles the exact same class of risk: Task 1 explicitly avoids touching deploy.sh/deploy.yml/deploy_test.yml because 'Деплой-манифесты — зона Task 2 и Task 5, они идут в этой же волне параллельно; правка их отсюда даст конфликт на ровном месте' (tasks/1.md ~line 218), and Task 3 explicitly declines to touch a stale docstring in _llm_common.py to avoid a Wave-1 merge conflict with Task 4 (tasks/3.md Edge cases). Task 6/Task 7 got no equivalent treatment even though the file overlap there is far larger (Task 7 rewrites most of the file) than the deploy-manifest or docstring cases that WERE flagged.
findings.fix: Either (a) explicitly forbid the t_hunted_source.py alias option in Task 6 and require the cap map to reference `t_hunted_source._IMAGE_LIMIT` by its existing private name (Task 6's own stated default already does this, so this just removes the tempting alternative), or (b) add an explicit cross-reference note to both Task 6 and Task 7 stating that any touch to t_hunted_source.py must land after Task 7's rewrite, mirroring the Task1↔Task2 and Task3↔Task4 precedent already used elsewhere in this same decomposition.

findings.issue: Task 6 (tasks/6.md, 'Files — правим': news_bot.py, ~2924-2995 and ~3388-3396 for the per-source cap map and its threading into publish_article) and Task 8 (tasks/8.md, 'Files': news_bot.py ~4291-4311 for the alignment-guard call site) are both Wave 3 tasks with no depends_on edge between them and both edit news_bot.py. Practical collision risk is low -- the two edit regions are roughly 900-1300 lines apart in a ~4900-line file, so a line-level patch conflict is unlikely -- but neither task's Dependencies or Edge-cases section acknowledges that the other is touching the same file in the same wave, which breaks this decomposition's own established pattern of calling out same-file/same-wave overlaps explicitly (see Task1↔Task2 on deploy manifests, Task3↔Task4 on _llm_common.py).
findings.fix: Add a one-line cross-reference in Task 6 and Task 8 noting the other also edits news_bot.py in the same wave, in different regions, so a reviewer merging both diffs knows to expect two independent hunks rather than investigate an unexpected second change to the file.
